dishes.dish: Bloody Mary Prawn Cocktail. Chilled prawns in a spiced tomato and vodka sauce, served in a glass with a celery-salt rim.

dishes.basis: Chicken braised in red wine (sulphites); flour to thicken and butter are common.

why.celery: Beef stock often includes celery as an aromatic.

Apples, celery and walnuts in mayonnaise (egg yolk).

Custard of cream and egg yolks under burnt sugar.

Cutlets dredged in flour, in a Marsala wine reduction, often finished with butter.
Cold soup of tomato, pepper and cucumber with bread and sherry vinegar.

why.nuts: Some versions use almonds; treated as uncertain.

dishes.basis: Leeks in a vinaigrette of Dijon mustard and wine vinegar; often topped with chopped egg.

why.sesame: Commercial buns often contain sesame seeds.

why.milk: Bao dough and filling often use evaporated or powdered milk.
why.molluscs: Char siu marinades commonly include oyster sauce.

dishes.basis: Chicken stew cooked in niter kibbeh (spiced butter), served with hard-boiled eggs; injera may be part wheat.

why.sulphites: Wine is often added to doro wat.

dishes.basis: Filo pie of spinach, feta and egg.
Bechamel of flour, butter, milk and egg yolk on top; the meat sauce often has wine.

Raw fish cured in lime juice.

why.crustaceans: Shrimp versions of ceviche are common.
why.molluscs: Octopus or squid is often used in ceviche.

why.eggs: Eggs are essential to the sponge cake.
